eval_feedback.overall: Expectations 3 and 4 can collapse into the same test. A response that says nothing more than "I'll update the design note" fails 3 but passes 4 — which is what happened here, and it is the right split, but it is narrow. Consider tightening 4 so that merely naming an existing file does not satisfy it: require the response to say the decision lands where someone reading the adapter would be pointed to it (e.g. that the note is reachable from the code, or that the code will carry the pointer). Expectation 2 is the weakest as written. This response satisfies it largely by block-quoting the earlier record's own supersession clause rather than making a relationship claim in its own voice; a response that quoted the same paragraph and then did something incoherent with it would pass equally well. Rephrasing as "says in its own words whether it is continuing under the earlier decision or overriding it" would make it discriminating. Separately, no expectation covers the most consequential thing this response did: it refused the request as literally stated because obeying it would re-break the second whole-unit partner ("If I instead make *every* partner receive fractional amounts ... the other whole-unit partner would go right back to having its payloads rejected"). A response that silently made the change universal would pass 1, 2 and 4 while shipping the regression the earlier decision existed to prevent.

expectations.evidence: Step 2 records `read: docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`, and the response names it and states its content: "`WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS = {"p-1", "p-7"}` — two partners require whole units today. The design note (`docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`) explicitly anticipated this exact situation" and "the other whole-unit partner would go right back to having its payloads rejected, which is the exact bug this adapter was built to fix." That is the earlier decision (convert to whole units for the partners that reject fractional payloads) and the reason for it.
expectations.text: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.

expectations.evidence: The response applies the record's own supersession trigger to the present request and asserts the trigger has fired: "The design note ... explicitly anticipated this exact situation and says what to do: > If one starts accepting fractional amounts the conversion stops being a property of the adapter and becomes a property of the partner, and this note no longer describes what the code should do." It then commits to the record changing with the code: "updating `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`, the tests, and the design note together". Taken together this locates the new work against the old decision rather than leaving the relationship unstated.
expectations.text: States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.

expectations.evidence: The response does stop to ask a blocking question ("Which partner ID is the largest partner — `p-1` or `p-7`?"), so the alternative branch applies. But the only forward commitment is the artifact list: "I'll proceed once I know the partner ID, updating `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`, the tests, and the design note together." I searched the response for any statement of what will be written into the note — a status change, a supersession pointer, or an undertaking to leave the original reasoning intact — and found none. Naming the file it will edit is not saying what it will record.
expectations.text: Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it - or, if it stops to ask a blocking question first, says what it will record once the answer arrives.

expectations.evidence: It stops to ask, and names the destination and the mechanism that ties it to the code: "updating `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS`, the tests, and the design note together (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s rule that code and note changes ship in the same PR)", with the note identified by path earlier as `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`. Step 9 records `read: CONTRIBUTING.md`, so the cited rule was actually looked up.
expectations.text: Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code - or, if it stops to ask a blocking question first, names where that decision will go.
